Hi Neha —

Appreciate the recap — yes, the items you list are what we need. A few clarifying questions for Rishi before we set up the deep dive:

- Do you store raw prompts submitted by end users anywhere persistent (longer than ephemeral buffers)?
- Do you persist generated outputs by default? If so, what is the default retention period and can it be shortened or turned off?
- Where is persisted data stored geographically (if retained)? Can we restrict to US-only or EU-only?
- What logging is available for audit (who queried what, request IDs, timestamps)? How long are audit logs retained by default?
- For Private deployments, can we use our own KMS/HSM and enforce that no plaintext keys are held by Redwood?

If you can provide short answers + links to SOC2/retention docs, that will help our security reviewers. We may also want to request a short architecture diagram showing data flow for inference.

Hi Aditi —

Thanks for the clear list — below are concrete answers (summary first, then short detail + links):

Summary answers:
- Raw prompts: NOT persisted to long-term storage by default for hosted API customers. Prompts are processed in memory and buffered briefly for inference; persistent logging of prompts is configurable and OFF by default.
- Generated outputs: By default, we persist request metadata and a conversation record for product/analytics/quality purposes; the text of outputs is retained for 30 days by default and can be shortened or disabled.
- Retention: Default retention for generated content and QA logs is 30 days. Customers can request shorter retention or no persistent logging on Hosted plans via support/contract. Dedicated/Private deployments allow full control of retention policies.
- Residency: Data storage region is configurable at the tenant level. Hosted customers can be pinned to US or EU regions; Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) keep all data in customer environment.
- Audit logs: We retain immutable audit logs (request IDs, timestamps, model versions, caller identity) for 90 days by default for hosted accounts; longer retention is available as an add-on.
- KMS/HSM: In Redwood Private, customers can use customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and we do not hold plaintext keys. For Dedicated, we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations.

Details and references:
- Prompt handling: Our inference runtime processes prompts in-memory and streams tokens to/from the model. For Hosted API, we have two logging modes: "transient-only" (no persistent transcript stored) and "persist-analytics" (stores anonymized transcripts/outputs for 30 days). The default for newly created production accounts is "persist-analytics" to enable quality monitoring; we can change this setting during onboarding or via contract.
- Output storage and minimization: We recommend customers implement client-side PII redaction before sending prompts when possible. For cases where the application needs raw PII in prompts (e.g., personalized responses), we offer pseudonymization tooling and a post-processing redaction hook.
- Residency controls: Tenant-data region is enforced at the object-store and block level and replicates only to selected regions (no cross-region replication by default unless configured).
- Logs & telemetry: Audit logs include request ID, caller (API key), route, model, token counts, and timestamp. Full request/response text is only included if persistent logging is enabled for the tenant.

Attachments and docs (attached to this email):
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC2-SR control summary)
- data-retention-policy-2026.pdf (retention defaults, config options)
- pseudonymization-process.png (high-level flow for PII minimization)

Recommended next steps:
1) If FinPay wants no persistent storage of prompts/outputs: use Hosted + request "transient-only" logging mode or deploy Redwood Private with BYOK; we can document the SOW changes.
2) Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive (Priyom can walk the inference flow and show where redaction hooks live).
3) Share any specific regulatory retention windows you must meet (e.g., 180 days for dispute logs) and we will confirm options/pricing.

If helpful, I can also provide the exact API parameter names for disabling transcript storage and a sample policy snippet for setting tenant retention to 7 days.
